### Why

- There is no registered written duty-manager permission for the extension. The 9 October request is still pending, and a pending request is expressly not permission.
- Changing the date now—even if the warehouse could move the box to reserve storage before 13:45 and charge the centre EUR 22—would be an unauthorised extension.
- Tomorrow’s approval sitting cannot cure today’s action. Permission obtained on 13 October would not retrospectively authorise a date change made on 12 October.
- By tomorrow’s sitting, the scheduled destruction will already have occurred and cannot be reversed.
- There is no authorised collection or other lawful hold available before destruction. Withdrawing the box from the manifest, leaving the full manifest unreleased, or manually instructing the warehouse to retain it would all bypass the established release and extension controls.

The uniqueness of the correspondence and photographs makes the outcome especially regrettable, but it does not create authority to disregard the policy. The appropriate response is to follow the authorised process and clearly record the pending request and the conflict for management review.

Operationally, the centre should afterwards examine why a documented request made on 9 October did not receive approval before the 12 October expiry—possibly through earlier approval handling, an emergency-hold procedure, or clearer notification when a pending request will miss the next sitting. But under the policy as given, those improvements do not authorise an exception today.
